Install the tempify Python backend

Source: R/tempify-install.R
install_tempify.Rd

Creates (or updates) a persistent Python virtual environment with the tempify package, which thermify then uses automatically in every session.

Usage

install_tempify(
  envname = tempify_envname(),
  requirement = tempify_requirement(),
  python_version = ">=3.10",
  restart_message = TRUE
)

Arguments

envname

Name of the virtual environment.

requirement

pip requirement for tempify. The default installs the current version from GitHub; a tag can be pinned, for example "tempify @ git+https://github.com/djwillichile/tempify@v0.1.6".

python_version

Python version used to create the environment when it does not exist, passed to reticulate::virtualenv_starter().

restart_message

Print the instructions to restart R?

Value

The path of the environment's Python, invisibly.

Details

You rarely need this function. With reticulate (>= 1.41) installed, thermify declares tempify when it is loaded in an interactive session, and the first time the tempify engine is used reticulate builds and caches a Python environment with it (this takes one or two minutes and downloads about 100 MB once). install_tempify() is the alternative when that automatic route is not available (older reticulate) or when you prefer a named, persistent environment.

The automatic setup runs only in interactive sessions, never while a package is being checked, and is skipped when you have already chosen a Python (RETICULATE_PYTHON, reticulate::use_python() and similar). Set the environment variable THERMIFY_TEMPIFY_AUTO=true (or options(thermify.tempify_auto = TRUE) before loading thermify) to enable it in scripts, or false to disable it.

Installing from GitHub needs git on the system path.

See also

tempify_available(), tempify_version()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
install_tempify()
# restart R, then
library(thermify)
tempify_available()
} # }
